questions.stem: The BRAIN of a computer is the:
questions.explanation: CPU = Central Processing Unit — executes instructions, does arithmetic & logic. Comprises ALU + CU + registers. ROM = Read-Only Memory (firmware). Hard disk / SSD = persistent storage. Monitor = output device.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.explanation: RAM — Random Access Memory. Volatile (lost on power-off), fast, stores data currently being processed. ROM — Read-Only Memory, non-volatile, stores firmware / BIOS. Typical laptops: 8-32 GB RAM, 256 GB - 2 TB SSD.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the FULL FORM with its ACRONYM. A. HTTP.  B. URL.  C. LAN.  D. SMTP. List-II: 1. Hypertext Transfer Protocol.  2. Uniform Resource Locator.  3. Local Area Network.  4. Simple Mail Transfer Protocol.
questions.explanation: HTTP — app-layer protocol for web. URL — address of a web resource. LAN — network within a limited area (vs WAN, MAN). SMTP — protocol for sending email. Bonus: POP3/IMAP — receiving email. FTP — File Transfer Protocol.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.explanation: Classical/binary: 1 KB = 2¹⁰ = 1,024 bytes. Decimal/SI: 1 kB = 1,000 bytes; 1 KiB = 1,024 bytes (IEC standard). In everyday use, 'KB' usually means 1,024 bytes. Hierarchy: B → KB → MB → GB → TB → PB.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The FATHER OF COMPUTER is considered to be:
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage — designed the Analytical Engine (1837), a general-purpose mechanical computer. Ada Lovelace wrote the first 'programs' for it. Turing formalised computability (Turing machine). Von Neumann designed the stored-program architecture. Berners-Lee invented the WWW.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of the following is an OPERATING SYSTEM?
questions.explanation: Linux — open-source OS (kernel by Linus Torvalds, 1991). Other OSes: Windows, macOS, Android, iOS. Word = application. Python = programming language. Chrome = web browser.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

options.option_text: Monitors and controls incoming/outgoing network traffic based on security rules

questions.explanation: Firewall — network-security device (hardware, software, or combination). Filters traffic to block unauthorised access. Works with antivirus + intrusion detection. Different from antivirus (file scanning) — can be deployed at router or OS level.
